abstract: Symbolic music generation often continues MIDI passages by predicting subsequent notes or events. Held-out prediction loss can overestimate generalization to unseen compositions when training contains another performance or arrangement of a test work. We introduce Multi-View Alignment-Aware Same-Work Identification, combining complementary musical representations with temporal alignment of shared passages to remove test-work versions from training while preserving unrelated material and fixing evaluation files. In a controlled cohort of 100 manually verified pairs selected for high embedding similarity, replacing 3.29% of training windows with test-work versions reduces mean per-group NLL by up to 30.16% relative to matched unrelated content. Across two datasets and two generators, our method brings test losses closest to a reference built from independent work labels. Compared with removing the same number of files at random, it leaves fewer test works exposed and retains more eligible content, including about 99% of eligible tokens on the piano-performance dataset. A separate study on that dataset matches training tokens and updates: no test works remain exposed under the dataset labels, and mean relative test loss is 2.15% higher than an independently selected reference. These findings support keeping all versions of each composition in one split when evaluating generalization to unseen works. The project is available at https://kunbai05-nb.github.io/.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文针对文件不重叠仍残留同作品版本并压低留出损失的问题，提出结合多视角检索与保序对齐及校准验证的 MVA-SWI ，在 100 组高相似对中替换 3.29% 训练窗口使 MIDI-GPT 组内平均 NLL 下降 30.16% 的敏感性证据下实现最接近独立标签参考的隔离，但 Table IV 随机划分审计在 LMD-clean 残留 17.75% 暴露，这与下游固定划分暴露 25/142 个测试作品约 17.61% 属不同口径，而干净保留略低与听感差异不显著构成主要代价。
originalTitle: Beyond File-Level Splits: Rethinking Symbolic Music Evaluation via Multi-View Alignment
readerTitle: 从文件去重到作品隔离：多视角对齐的符号音乐评测清洗
